concept: This is a comeback story, so the deck is built as a three-act chase. The hero sets Pakistan's 337 in muted grey and lets India's answer land in white, with '1 wicket to spare' as the hook. Slide 2 is the low point as one giant number, 252/8, so the reader feels how lost the game looked. Slide 3 answers it with Mohit Ulva's 49* as an equally giant number, the heist. Slide 4 shows the four innings that made the runs as bars, so the base and the finish sit side by side. Slide 5 explains why in three lines and ends on a question. Cricket blue, type and bars only, no photos or logos.
caption:
Pakistan made 337. India chased it down with one wicket left.

India's U19 side are Asia Cup champions after a last-over finish in Oman. Captain Lakshya Raichandani (80 off 101) and Aaryavir Sehwag (58) kept the chase alive, but wickets kept falling, and at 252/8 India still needed 86.

Then Mohit Ulva: 49 not out off 26 balls. Fast enough that the tail never had to survive long, and India got home against the defending champions.
